faq.q: What are the most common squash injuries?
faq.a: Squash means hard lunges, fast turns and quick changes of direction. Common complaints include rolled ankles, front-of-knee pain from lunging, shoulder pain, wrist or elbow niggles, and lower back pain.

faq.q: When should I get a squash injury checked?
faq.a: If pain keeps coming back, stops you moving normally, or has not settled, talk it through with a registered physiotherapist. Get urgent care for severe pain, a joint that looks out of place, numbness, or if you cannot put weight on a leg. In an emergency, call 911.

faq.q: Can a physiotherapist assess a squash injury on video?
faq.a: Yes. A Calm Joints video assessment is with a registered physiotherapist. They look at how you move and talk through next steps with you, including whether an in-person visit makes sense. Book a time that fits around your matches.
